Search this TypeScript/Node codebase at /tmp/ruflo for cacheable repeated expensive work that is currently NOT cached — pure or near-pure computations recomputed on every call. EXCLUDE /node_modules, /.git, /dist, /tests, *.test.ts, *.spec.ts.

Find concretely:
1. Repeated file reads + JSON.parse of the SAME static/config file across multiple code paths or across calls (package.json, tsconfig, claude-flow.config.json, plugin manifests, registry JSON, lock files) — these are read-once-per-process candidates.
2. Repeated synchronous O(n²)/O(n log n) computations: sorts, groupBy, uniq, similarity/distance matrices, graph traversals, path canonicalization, repeated `fs.readdirSync` over a directory tree, repeated regex compilation (`new RegExp`), repeated `JSON.stringify` of stable objects for hashing.
3. Embedding/vector computation of identical inputs (same text → same vector) recomputed; cosine/inner-product over the same pair set; HNSW rebuild on unchanged data.
4. Repeated network/registry fetches: the plugin registry from IPFS/Pinata, npm metadata, git refs — fetched fresh on every call when they could be cached with a TTL.
5. Repeated `child_process` spawns (`execSync`, `spawnSync`) of deterministic commands (e.g. `git rev-parse`, `npm ls`, `node --version`, `gh api`) whose output is stable for the process/commit.
6. Distance/similarity/levenshtein recomputed on the same strings.
7. Per-call topology/strategy enum→metadata lookups building a fresh map each call.
8. Regex or parser constructed inside a hot function instead of module-scope constant.

Method: ripgrep then read.
  rg -n 'JSON\.parse\(fs\.|fs\.readFileSync|readFileSync' /tmp/ruflo/v3 -g '!node_modules' -g '!*.test.ts'
  rg -n 'execSync|spawnSync|execFileSync' /tmp/ruflo/v3 -g '!node_modules' -g '!*.test.ts'
  rg -n 'new RegExp\(' /tmp/ruflo/v3 -g '!node_modules' -g '!*.test.ts'
  rg -n '\.sort\(|\.reduce\(|new Map\(' /tmp/ruflo/v3 -g '!node_modules' -g '!*.test.ts'
  rg -n 'cosineSimilarity|distance|levenshtein|cosine' /tmp/ruflo/v3 -g '!node_modules' -g '!*.test.ts'
  rg -n 'fetch\(|got\(|axios|https?\.get' /tmp/ruflo/v3 -g '!node_modules' -g '!*.test.ts'

Hot files:
  v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/plugins/store/discovery.ts (registry fetch)
  v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/ruvector/*.ts
  v3/@claude-flow/memory/src/hnsw-index.ts, agentdb-adapter.ts
  v3/@claude-flow/embeddings/src/embedding-service.ts
  v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/*.ts (doctor.ts, init/*.ts — lots of sync fs/exec)
  v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/init/executor.ts
  bin/cli.js

For each finding return: file path, line number(s), 6-12 line excerpt, what is recomputed and roughly how often (per-command? per-record? per-render?), the input shape that makes it cacheable (same input → same output — yes/no invalidation concerns), an estimated cost (file I/O, spawn, O(n²) over N), and a concrete fix (module-level `let cache` / `WeakMap` / `lru-cache` / memoize fn with a TTL; lazy-init-on-first-call; cache keyed by file mtime or content hash). Call out invalidation pitfalls explicitly. 8-15 findings. Verify excerpts against actual files — do not guess.
